samples.summary: An involuntary 401 erases the local live entries, which include the un-pushed change log — destroying the only durable copy of unsent work
samples.evidence: `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm calls `logout({... eraseLocalData: "keep-archives"})`, which reaches `dropAllForUser(userId, {keepArchives:true})` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1031). That loop calls `this.purge(docKey)` for every header, and `purge` deletes the CHANGES range as well as the snapshot. The justification in the comment — "The live entries still go. They are copies of content the server holds, so nothing is lost by dropping them" — is false for the log: the store's own eviction logic says the opposite (`evictOldest` skips any entry with `changeCount > 0` because "this store cannot tell an acked change from an unacked one", wafflebase-doc-store.ts). So a session that expires (or any transient 401 from a restarted backend) while a durable document holds un-pushed edits deletes exactly the work the feature exists to preserve; the redirect to /login is refusable (see the `redirectTo` comment about `beforeunload`, auth.ts:47-60), so the tab can keep running and then lose the edits on the next reload.

samples.summary: After a sign-out erase the still-mounted durable client re-persists the document to disk; the only write guard is the preference, not the sign-out
samples.evidence: The store is built with `isPersistenceEnabled: getOfflinePersistenceEnabled` and nothing else. `refuseIfDisabled` therefore only blocks writes when the *preference* is off. On the 401 path, `dropAllForUser` purges the entries and marks them evicted, so the client's next `appendChange` throws — which makes the SDK write a fresh `saveSnapshot`, and `saveSnapshot` does `this.evicted.delete(docKey)` and writes the document back (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:580-600). Because the 401 redirect is refusable (auth.ts:47-60: a `beforeunload` guard — which the sync chip registers precisely when there are unsent edits — lets the user cancel and the page keeps running), the erase promised on sign-out is undone and a signed-out account's document content is back on a possibly shared disk, with nothing scheduled to remove it again.

samples.summary: An election is acquired but never used when eligibility rises after the provider latched non-durable, holding the per-document lock and denying durability to every other tab
samples.evidence: `held.current` is written once per `subject` (`${me.id}:${docKey}`) on the first `ready` render and never revisited (collab-document-provider.tsx:242-248), while `useDurableDocument` keeps re-deciding: its `latched` eligibility is allowed to *rise* (use-durable-document.ts:159-163) and the effect then calls `acquireDurableSession` and holds `wb-durable:{user}:{docKey}` until unmount. So when the preference is switched on while a document is open — which is the chip's own primary entry point (`turnOnOfflineSaving`, sync-status-chip.tsx:148) — this tab takes and keeps the election for a document it will never persist. Any other tab that opens the same document is refused the election (`acquireDurableSession` returns undefined) and stays non-durable, so the feature the user just enabled silently does not work for that document in any tab until the holding tab closes it.

samples.summary: The fallback store created by the preference watcher is never closed, leaking an open IndexedDB connection per toggle-off
samples.evidence: `const current = store() ?? new WafflebaseDocStore({ userId: who });` — when the fallback branch is taken (the documented common case, since Settings is where the toggle lives and the runtime's store is normally supplied, but any path with no store hits it) the new store is used for `eraseOfflineData` and never `close()`d. Every other caller in this file (`eraseOfflineDataOnLogout`, `retryPendingOfflineErase`, `purgeOfflineDocuments`, `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments`) closes in a `finally`. A lingering open connection is what blocks a later `deleteDatabase`/version change, which is the case `open()`'s `onblocked` arm rejects on.

samples.summary: `lost` / `writesFailing` / `persistDisabled` are latched per component instance, not per document, so one document's loss can mark a later document non-durable
samples.evidence: `useState(false)` for all three, with no reset keyed on `clientKey`/document. If `CollabDocumentProvider` stays mounted at the same tree position across a `docKey` change (its `held`/`subject` logic explicitly contemplates re-deciding in place), the new document inherits the previous one's latched verdict and `durable` stays false forever — the chip reports `not-saved` and re-registers the unload guard for a document that is in fact being persisted. Under-reporting is the safe direction, but the state is wrong for the new document.

samples.summary: `retryPendingOfflineErase()` on mount can erase the entries of the user who is signing in, racing a document opened in the same render
samples.evidence: `OfflineRuntime` is mounted by `PrivateRoute` alongside `<Outlet />`, so a deep link to `/s/:id` mounts the editor and this effect together. If the signed-in user has an owed erase recorded from a previous failed sign-out, `retryPendingOfflineErase` runs `dropAllForUser` for *that same user id* while the durable client for the just-opened document is already writing — purging its entry and adding the key to the shared `evicted` set, so the next append throws and the document drops out of `saved-locally`. The owed erase is for stale pre-sign-out content, but it is not scoped to exclude entries this session has just created.

samples.summary: `return null` while the identity query is pending blanks the editor for an anonymous visitor on a public route that is not wrapped in NonDurableScope
samples.evidence: `identified = !mayPersist || !identityPending;` and `if (!ready) return null;`. `mayPersist` is true whenever the build supports client keys, the preference is on, and `permitted` is true — which is the default everywhere except `shared-document.tsx`. On any other public/unauthenticated surface that renders `CollabDocumentProvider` (e.g. a template landing/preview) with no `['me']` cache to seed `initialData`, the whole editor subtree renders `null` until `/auth/me` answers, rather than rendering on the ambient client. The doc comment claims "an anonymous visitor waits for nothing", which only holds for routes that opted into `NonDurableScope`.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. fetchWithAuth's 401 arm (auth.ts:250-267) calls logout with eraseLocalData:"keep-archives", which flows through logout's unconditional `await eraseOfflineDataOnLogout({keepArchives:true})` (auth.ts:125-127) and offline-erase.ts:200-232/26-32 into WafflebaseDocStore.dropAllForUser(userId,{keepArchives:true}) (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1031-1074). That loop calls `await this.purge(docKey)` for every header key of the user (line 1050) with no exception for entries whose change log is non-empty; keepArchives only skips dropArchivesWhere (1071-1073). purge deletes the CHANGES range along with snapshot and header (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:827-835, esp. 832), outright and without archiving. The comment's premise that live entries are "copies of content the server holds" is contradicted by the store's own evictOldest, which refuses any candidate with changeCount > 0 precisely because "this store cannot tell an acked change from an unacked one … a non-empty log counts as unsent" (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1332-1362). Archiving only occurs in remove() when expectLoss was latched (757-812, archive written only `if (record && losing)`), and the sole latch source is the SDK's local-changes-dropped subscription (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:217-220) — nothing on the 401/logout path archives before purging, and after the purge the snapshot record is gone so a later remove() archives nothing. The path is reachable in normal use: a 401 requires a reachable server, i.e. an expired cookie or restarted backend while a durable document holds un-pushed edits, and the redirect is documented as refusable via the beforeunload unsaved-changes guard (auth.ts:47-74), so the tab keeps running with its only durable copy already deleted. I found no guard anywhere that spares entries with pending log rows on this path. Data loss of unsent work on a real path is squarely in the correctness lane and blocking.

finding.summary: After a sign-out erase the still-mounted durable client re-persists the document to disk; the only write guard is the preference, not the sign-out
finding.evidence: The store is built with `isPersistenceEnabled: getOfflinePersistenceEnabled` and nothing else. `refuseIfDisabled` therefore only blocks writes when the *preference* is off. On the 401 path, `dropAllForUser` purges the entries and marks them evicted, so the client's next `appendChange` throws — which makes the SDK write a fresh `saveSnapshot`, and `saveSnapshot` does `this.evicted.delete(docKey)` and writes the document back (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:580-600). verdict.reason: The finding is accurate in the repository. The durable store is constructed with `isPersistenceEnabled: getOfflinePersistenceEnabled` as its only write gate (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:131-149), and `refuseIfDisabled` throws solely on that preference (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:382-391). Nothing in the sign-out path changes the preference (only Settings page.tsx:128 and sync-status-chip.tsx:149 call the setter), so after `dropAllForUser` purges and marks keys evicted (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1050-1057), a still-mounted client's next `saveSnapshot` passes the only guard, clears the eviction mark and re-writes the snapshot/header back to disk (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:580-600). The repo's own test asserts this rewrite hazard is blocked only when the preference is off (wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts:796-829), leaving the sign-out case unprotected. The page can survive the sign-out redirect: `redirectTo` is documented and latch-released precisely because a `beforeunload` guard can refuse it (api/auth.ts:47-74), the chip registers such a guard in `saving`/`not-saved` (sync-status-chip.tsx:171-182, reachable for a durable document via sync-state.ts:87), and the 401 arm calls `logout({eraseLocalData:'keep-archives'})` before that refusable redirect (api/auth.ts:250-269). After a full erase the identity is spent (offline-erase.ts:215-223), so no later logout/purge can name the account and only the 30-day sweep would remove the re-written content. No guard elsewhere makes this unreachable — `watchForOfflineDisable` fires only on the preference's falling edge (offline-erase.ts:380-425) and OfflineRuntime installs no sign-out write gate (offline-runtime.tsx:59-162). Broken erase invariant with content restored to a possibly shared disk is in the correctness lane.

Any other tab that opens the same document is refused the election (`acquireDurableSession` returns undefined) and stays non-durable, so the feature the user just enabled silently does not work for that document in any tab until the holding tab closes it.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. use-durable-document.ts:161-163 upgrades the latched eligibility when the preference rises during an open document; that changes `subject` (line 179), which is an effect dep (line 214), so the effect re-runs into the acquire branch and holds `wb-durable:{user}:{docKey}` via acquireDurableSession (line 198) until unmount. Meanwhile CollabDocumentProvider's own latch key is `${me?.id ?? 'anon'}:${docKey}` (collab-document-provider.tsx:229) — it contains no preference term — and `held.current` is only rewritten when that subject changes (lines 242-244), so `decided` stays `{durable:false, clientKey:undefined}` and line 277 renders the ambient non-durable branch forever. Nothing releases it: standDown is reachable only through onLockRefused/giveUp (lines 236-239, 296). The lock is origin-wide with `{ifAvailable:true}` (durable-session.ts:93-97), so any other tab opening the same document gets `undefined` and stays non-durable (behavior asserted by collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:217-230). The trigger is a first-class UI path: sync-status-chip.tsx:148-158 flips the preference while the editor is mounted, and offline-persistence-preference.ts:72,115-121 propagates it synchronously to the open document's hook. Existing tests cover only the falling case (use-durable-document.test.tsx:172-196; collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:310-330), not the rise. No guard, caller, or scope makes this unreachable; it is a state/invariant correctness defect in my lane (election held without the state that authorizes it, denying the feature to all other tabs for that document).

finding.summary: Turning the offline toggle off erases the disk, but the still-mounted durable client immediately re-writes every open document back to it
finding.evidence: `watchForOfflineDisable` (offline-erase.ts:346) calls `eraseOfflineData` → `WafflebaseDocStore.dropAllForUser`, which `purge()`s every key **and** adds each to `this.evicted` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:963-970). By deliberate design (`collab-document-provider.tsx:204-228`, `use-durable-document.ts:134-164`) the durable client is NOT torn down when the preference flips — it stays mounted for the life of the open document. Its next `appendChange` finds no header, hits `refuseIfEvicted` and throws (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:608-610, 665-674); the store's own doc-comment states the purpose of that throw is to make the SDK "poison the log and write a fresh snapshot". That fresh `saveSnapshot` re-creates the snapshot/header rows and clears the evicted mark (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:549-554). Net effect: seconds after the user switches the setting off, the document they had open is back on disk, and no further preference change will ever fire to remove it (the listener only acts on a true→false edge). The Settings copy that promises "turning it off deletes what was stored" is therefore false for exactly the document the user was looking at. Nothing in the erase path detaches, disables, or stops the live store.

verdict.reason: The finding's core premise ("Nothing in the erase path detaches, disables, or stops the live store") is false. The live durable store the SDK writes through is constructed with `isPersistenceEnabled: getOfflinePersistenceEnabled` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:146, passed as `store={store}` at :175 — the only non-test store given to the SDK). Every write entry point calls `refuseIfDisabled` as its first statement, before any deflate or IndexedDB transaction: saveSnapshot (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:581), appendChange (:623), saveMeta (:670); refuseIfDisabled (:382-391) throws and reports a write failure when the preference is off. So the claimed chain — appendChange throws via refuseIfEvicted, SDK writes a fresh snapshot, saveSnapshot re-creates the header/snapshot rows and clears the evicted mark (:593-598) — never reaches line 593: saveSnapshot throws at :581. The preference read is live (offline-persistence-preference.ts:40-58) and setOfflinePersistenceEnabled persists the value/mirror at :63-70 *before* dispatching the event watchForOfflineDisable listens on (offline-erase.ts:395), so the refusal is in effect from the instant of the flip, with no window before the erase. The refusal is also surfaced to the durability chip via onWriteFailure (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:140), so it does not silently over-report. Existing tests pin precisely this scenario (wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts:796-829: "refuses to write the open document back to the disk it just cleared" — all three writes reject and load stays undefined after dropAllForUser). Ground: already-guarded.

finding.summary: The owed-erase marker is a single localStorage slot that any later sign-out clears or overwrites, so one account's documents can be left on a shared device forever
finding.evidence: `PENDING_ERASE_KEY` holds at most one user id. In `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` both success branches call `rememberPendingErase(undefined)` unconditionally (offline-erase.ts:169 and 172) — they do not check that the recorded owed id is the user this erase was for. Sequence: user A signs out, the IndexedDB erase throws, `rememberPendingErase("A")` (line 178). User B signs in; `retryPendingOfflineErase` also fails (it swallows and keeps the marker, line 208-210). B's session expires → `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm calls `logout({eraseLocalData:"keep-archives"})` → B's erase succeeds → `rememberPendingErase(undefined)` wipes the marker that named **A**. A's live entries and archives stay on the disk with nothing left that can name them. The same single slot also means a second failing logout (`rememberPendingErase(who)`) silently overwrites a still-owed erase for a different account.

verdict.reason: The finding describes a single-slot pending-erase marker cleared unconditionally by any later sign-out, but the repository implements a per-user set. PENDING_ERASE_KEY (offline-erase.ts:122) is written as a JSON array via writePendingErases (offline-erase.ts:152-163, using JSON.stringify([...new Set(ids)]) at :157) and read by pendingErases() (offline-erase.ts:131-150), which parses the array and falls back to [raw] for the legacy bare-string form so an upgrade loses nothing. The claimed evidence lines are misquoted: offline-erase.ts:166-168 is the definition of rememberPendingErase(userId: string), which APPENDS ([...pendingErases(), userId]) and cannot be called with undefined; lines 170-172 are a doc comment, not calls. Both success branches of eraseOfflineDataOnLogout call forgetPendingErase(who) (offline-erase.ts:219 and :222), which removes only that id via filter((id) => id !== userId) (offline-erase.ts:177), so B's successful logout cannot wipe A's owed marker. The failure path appends per-user (offline-erase.ts:228), so a second failing logout does not overwrite another account's owed erase. retryPendingOfflineErase (offline-erase.ts:245-265) loops over every owed id, forgetting only ids whose own erase succeeded (:258) and keeping failures queued (:259-260). The precise A-fails-then-B-succeeds sequence is covered by a passing test (offline-erase.test.ts:316-342), as is the two-owed-ids case (offline-erase.test.ts:344-364). The described code is not present in this working tree.

finding.summary: The session reconcile purges any stored document missing from a listing it fetched earlier, racing documents another tab created or has open
finding.evidence: `OfflineRuntime` fetches `fetchDocuments()` (offline-runtime.tsx:114) and then `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments(...)` deletes every stored document id **not** in that list, with `archives: "drop"` (offline-erase.ts:281-286). The IndexedDB database is shared across tabs and `storedDocumentIds()` is scoped only by user, so it includes entries written by *another tab of the same user*. A document created (or first persisted) in tab A after tab B's `/documents` response returns is absent from B's list and present in B's store scan, so B purges it. `WafflebaseDocStore.purge` (line 781) — unlike `dropAllForUser` — neither consults `isLive`/`isOpenElsewhere` nor adds the key to `evicted`, so tab A's subsequent `appendChange` finds no header, returns the contract's silent "no base" success, and every later edit goes nowhere while tab A's chip still reports `saved-locally`. That is precisely the silent-loss failure the eviction and collection paths go to lengths to avoid; this path has none of those guards.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. The reconcile call at offline-erase.ts:355-361 does not purge unconditionally: it passes skipOpen: true and updatedSince: options.listedAt alongside archives: "drop", and offline-runtime.tsx:127-133 stamps listedAt BEFORE await fetchDocuments() and supplies isOpenElsewhere: isOpenInAnyTab — the exact cross-tab race the finding describes. In purgeDocument (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:869-906) each candidate key is skipped when isLive(key) is true (line 886, which consults touched plus isOpenElsewhere at 397-402) and skipped when updatedAt(key) >= updatedSince (887-892); since header updatedAt is set to now on creation and every append (lines 590, 648, 686), a document another tab created or edited after the listing was requested is spared by both guards. isOpenInAnyTab (durable-session.ts:210-231) also fails safe, returning true when the Web Locks API is unavailable or the query throws. The claim that the purge "neither consults isLive/isOpenElsewhere nor adds the key to evicted" is wrong for the code on this path: purge is at line 827 (not 781) and is a private helper the reconcile never calls directly; its caller purgeDocument does this.evicted.add(key) at line 899, which is what makes a later append throw loudly at 712-716 instead of returning the contract's silent "no base" success. The cited offline-erase.ts:281-286 is a different function (purgeOfflineDocuments, the post-delete purge) which deliberately omits the guards because the server already confirmed the deletion.
